steps.title: Prepare Lysis Buffer
steps.instruction: In each 2 mL microcentrifuge tube add 650 µL Buffer A, 650 µL Buffer B, 260 µL Buffer C, 175 µL 1 % (v/v) PVP, and 10 µL Proteinase K; mix and split the mixture equally into two 2 mL tubes (one tube serves two samples).

steps.title: Preheat Lysis Buffer
steps.instruction: Place the tubes on a hot plate and heat to 65 °C; pre‑heated solutions are less viscous and split more easily.

steps.title: Freeze and Grind Tissue
steps.instruction: Immerse a mortar and pestle in liquid nitrogen until fully chilled, add fungi with an ethanol‑cleaned spatula (grab only fungal tissue, minimal agar), place ~100 mg of frozen tissue into each tube, and grind to a fine powder for up to 1 minute, adding liquid nitrogen a little at a time to keep the mortar cold.

steps.title: Incubate Lysate at 65 °C
steps.instruction: Incubate the tubes for 30 minutes at 65 °C, mixing by inversion frequently (every 2–5 minutes) and opening the caps slightly to relieve any pressure generated by heat expansion.

steps.title: Add Potassium Acetate
steps.instruction: Add 280 µL 5 M potassium acetate to each tube, mix by inversion, then place the tubes on ice for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Phenol‑Chloroform Extraction
steps.instruction: Add 500–700 µL phenol:chloroform:isoamyl alcohol (PCI) 25:24:1 (as much as the tube can reasonably hold), mix by inversion for >5 minutes or vortex briefly (5–10 s), incubate 2 minutes at room temperature, and if the tube is over‑filled discard excess liquid onto a napkin.

substeps.instruction: Mix by inversion >5 min or vortex 5–10 s.
If over‑filled, tip out excess onto a napkin.

steps.title: Centrifuge and Collect Aqueous Phase
steps.instruction: Spin the tubes at 6000 × g for 10 minutes, then transfer the upper aqueous supernatant to a new 2 mL tube.

steps.title: Chloroform‑Isoamyl Wash
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume of chloroform:isoamyl alcohol (CI) 24:1 (≈1000 µL) to the transferred supernatant, using autoclaved cut pipette tips to avoid DNA shearing.

steps.title: Mix and Incubate CI Wash
steps.instruction: Invert the tube for 5 minutes, then incubate at room temperature for 2 minutes.

steps.title: RNase Treatment and Optional CI Washes
steps.instruction: Transfer the supernatant (≈700 µL) to a new 2 mL tube, add 2.5 µL RNase A, and incubate at 37 °C for 1.5–2 hours; optionally perform 1–2 additional CI washes to increase purity.

steps.title: Precipitate DNA
steps.instruction: Add 1/10 volume of 3 M sodium acetate (e.g., 75 µL for 750 µL total volume), mix, then add 1 volume of isopropanol (equal to the total volume after acetate addition).

steps.title: Incubate for DNA Threads
steps.instruction: Gently invert to mix and incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes; DNA will appear as visible threads or a sugary‑looking solution.

steps.title: Pellet DNA by Centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 3000 × g for 2 minutes, then slowly pour off the supernatant, keeping the tube orientation consistent to avoid disturbing the pellet.

steps.title: Ethanol Wash
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL freshly prepared cold 70 % (v/v) ethanol to the pellet, then centrifuge at 3000 × g for 2 minutes, pipette out the ethanol and remove as much as possible.

substeps.instruction: Pipette out ethanol, remove residual liquid.

steps.title: Dry Pellet
steps.instruction: Dry the pellet at room temperature for 10–15 minutes, or at 65 °C for <2 minutes, or place in a vacuum chamber for 10–20 minutes to remove remaining ethanol.

steps.title: Resuspend DNA
steps.instruction: Resuspend the dried pellet in 50–100 µL TE buffer (pH 9) at 65 °C; if protein contamination is high, add 600–800 µL TE at 65 °C, resuspend, add an equal volume of CI, mix as in step 9, and then continue without the RNase and CI steps.

steps.title: Prepare Agarose Gel
steps.instruction: Make a 0.8–1 % agarose gel containing 3 µL ethidium bromide per 100 mL gel.

steps.title: Run Gel and Visualize
steps.instruction: Mix equal parts loading dye and DNA sample, load samples and a DNA ladder into wells, run the gel at 75–120 V for 45–60 minutes (or until the front has migrated 3/4 of the gel), then visualize bands under UV light.

steps.title: Optional High‑Yield Combination
steps.instruction: For applications requiring large DNA amounts, combine extracts from multiple tubes of the same sample, then measure the final concentration; for very clean DNA, perform additional CI washes (step 12b), noting that yield may decrease.

steps.title: Heat Water Bath to 37 °C
steps.instruction: Heat a water bath to 37 °C for use in the RNase treatment step.
